```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a paying customer within 90 days, so willingness to pay is the deciding test. B's comparable, SwagUp, publishes paid tiers ($99, $499 and $999 per month plus fulfillment fees). Named companies (Endcrawl via Printfection, BurnRate and Hampton via SwagUp) are documented paying for exactly this outcome. A's brief shows the opposite: every listed competitor is free or donation-supported, and the best-resourced one (Fakespot) shut down rather than sustain itself.",
    "B's payer is a business with a budget line (onboarding and marketing). A's payer is an individual consumer being asked to pay for something four installed alternatives provide free. That is a much harder first sale for one person.",
    "A's demand evidence is frustration quotes pulled from builders' own launch threads. None of it signals purchase intent, and it includes an explicit moral backlash ('downright immoral'). B's demand evidence comes from buyers describing a need they already spent money to solve.",
    "B's biggest weakness is that incumbents already offer the Stripe/Zapier-trigger mechanic, so there is no clear wedge. But that proves the market pays for it. A's weakness, no evidence anyone pays at all, directly blocks the 90-day goal.",
    "B's operational risks are real: physical fulfillment, customs and thin reseller margins. They can be contained for a first customer by reselling through an existing fulfillment API. A's risks can't be engineered away quickly: unsolved detection accuracy, false-positive backlash, and platform control by Reddit."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's price anchor. The '~$4.99/month typical consumer extension subscription' figure is unsourced and counts as missing. The only sourced comparable, GPTZero's $10-15 individual tier, is a different product for a different buyer (standalone AI-text detection). Nothing in the brief shows any user of a Reddit or review filter paying any amount.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B wins mainly because it has documented paying buyers and A has none. B's brief still leaves the wedge against SwagUp/Zapier unresolved and lacks per-package unit economics. Its customs-friction claim is also cited without a source, and Stitchi/Swag.com pricing was not found. B is the better first bet on evidence, but it could still fail on margin or differentiation."
}
```
